privacy.heading: Private by design, not by promise
privacy.body: Nothing you type is ever sent anywhere — it's saved only in this browser, on this device. Your photos never pass through this app at all: they stay wherever you keep them, linked only by the item number you write down yourself, which is also how you name the files when you send them on. Keep a copy of your photos, your walkthrough video and this app's backup file somewhere that isn't this house — a phone in the building is not a second copy. And because nothing here is encrypted or password-protected, anyone who can use this device and browser can open it, so keep it somewhere only you can reach.

cards.title: Zero network requests
cards.body: The app is a single file that runs entirely in your browser, on your device. It makes no connections and loads nothing from the internet. You can run it with Wi-Fi off.

cards.title: Never a password
cards.body: By design, it never asks for or stores passwords or PINs. It records that accounts exist and where your written instructions live — the map, never the keys.

cards.title: Yours forever
cards.body: One-time purchase. The file is yours, works offline for life, and will still open years from now, exactly as it does today.

priceCard.sub: the one private place to inventory what you own line by line, track your policy, your claim, your deadlines and every extra cost, and print one packet for your adjuster — the searchable, totalled half your camera roll can't be.
bullets: 49 guided tasks across 7 phases — opening with a First 72 Hours phase for anyone standing in the middle of a loss, which you skip outright if nothing has happened yet

A room-by-room inventory that does the arithmetic: quantity times cost-each with a live line total, so a drawer of socks is one row — plus category, brand/model/serial, age, condition, proof type, loss status and replacement status
A Rooms tab that tracks every room's status and counts what's done, so the job is finishable in twenty-minute pieces instead of one impossible afternoon
A policy register that holds each coverage line, your deductible, and every scheduled item or special limit — in the figures from your own declarations page
A claim and payment record: one line per thing that happens, each payment tagged to its coverage and to where the money went, totalled as you go
A Dates & Deadlines tab for every date you're given, with who told you and when
A living-expense log that computes the increase over what you'd normally spend, line by line
A claim communication log, a contractor and adjuster directory with each estimate's date and amount, and a notes section for coverage details and what happened
A one-click printable Claim Packet — everything above on one page for your adjuster, with item numbers to name your photo files against

crossSell.heading: Organizing more than your home?
crossSell.body: Tenth Quietkeep organizer and a genuinely new buyer moment — insurance and preparedness search intent, not the estate/divorce family.
